lesson: Weight cues that worked best were broad lexical retrieval heads/MLP clusters, not arithmetic: the passed compass cluster at L52u[13277,3393,3390] dropped compass_turn by 0.403 while control moved only 0.021.

High OV contrast alone was not enough: L53H23 had strong global scores (digits 0.142, months 0.127, weekdays 0.119, code 0.108) but failed on weekday_offset with 0.0 target drop and even hurt compass_turn by 0.119.

Month and weekday retrieval candidates looked real in weights but still failed as skill parts: L41H9 scored month_number 0.074 in weights yet only dropped month_number by 0.037, and L51u5864 scored weekday-name support yet only dropped weekday_number by 0.059.

Parity-looking units were especially unreliable: L51u189 and L53u6838 both had strong odd/even asymmetry in weights, but the best screen there gave integer_parity -0.153 or -0.012, far below the 0.15 threshold and not better than random.

Some parts had large collateral damage without targeting the skill: L35H30 was strong in weights for boolean/code/weekday, but screening gave weekday_offset +0.667 and random same-size parts often matched the target drop (0.236).

Use control drops as a sanity check: when target effects were weak (e.g. L59H29 integer_comparison -0.009), random parts were comparable or larger, while the successful compass cluster had a clean gap (0.403 target vs 0.021 control).
